'''Kenneth Lamont''' '''Bazemore Jr.''' (born July 1, 1989) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]]. As a junior at [[Old Dominion Monarchs basketball|Old Dominion University]] in 2010–11, Bazemore won the [[Lefty Driesell Award]], an award given to the best defensive player in college basketball.

==College career==
Bazemore, a 6'5" [[shooting guard]] from [[Kelford, North Carolina]],<ref name="college">{{cite web|title=Kent Bazemore Player Profile|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Kent_Bazemore/Summary/18858|work=RealGM.com|access-date=January 29, 2014}}</ref> [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] the [[2007–08 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2007–08 season]]. As a freshman in [[2008–09 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2008–09]], Bazemore was a key rotation player for the Monarchs, averaging 4.5 points and 3.1 rebounds per game<ref name="college"/> as ODU won the [[2009 CollegeInsider.com Tournament]]. As a sophomore, he moved into the starting lineup and was a driving force for the [[Colonial Athletic Association]] regular-season and tournament champions. Bazemore averaged 8.4 points, 3.4 assists, 4.2 rebounds and 1.9 steals per game. He was named to the CAA All-Defensive team that season.<ref>[http://www.odusports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=31100&ATCLID=208421973 Kent Bazemore Profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222231941/http://www.odusports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=31100&ATCLID=208421973 |date=February 22, 2016 }}, accessed November 19, 2011</ref>

As a junior, Old Dominion repeated as tournament champions and made the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011 NCAA tournament]], losing to eventual national runner-up [[2010–11 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] 60–58. Bazemore averaged career highs of 12.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.2 steals per game and was named the CAA Defensive player of the year and second team All-Conference.  He also gained national recognition, receiving the Lefty Driesell Award given to the nation's top defensive player.<ref>[http://www.dailypress.com/sports/dp-spt-odu-bazemore-04012011,0,5570493.story ODU's Bazemore named Driesell National Defensive Player of the Year] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903075846/http://www.dailypress.com/sports/dp-spt-odu-bazemore-04012011,0,5570493.story |date=September 3, 2014 }}, accessed November 19, 2011</ref>

Prior to the [[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011–12 season]] Bazemore was named the CAA preseason player of the year.<ref>[http://www.caasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=8500&ATCLID=205318205 Drexel picked to win CAA men's basketball championship in 2011-12] accessed November 19, 2011</ref>  He was also named a preseason Mid-Major All-American by collegeinsider.com.<ref>[http://www.collegeinsider.com/henson/ The 2011-12 Lou Henson preseason All-America team], accessed November 19, 2011</ref> In his final season at ODU, Bazemore averaged 15.4 points, 6.1 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game.

At halftime of a game against state rival [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] on December 10, 2016, Old Dominion retired Bazemore's #24 Monarchs jersey and inducted him into the school's athletic Ring of Honor.<ref>{{cite news|last=Brown|first=Mitch|url=http://wtkr.com/2016/12/10/monarchs-drop-a-heartbreaker-to-vcu-67-64-on-bazemore-night/|title=Monarchs drop a heartbreaker to VCU 67-64 on Bazemore Night|work=wtkr.com|date=December 10, 2016|access-date=December 14, 2016}}</ref>

Bazemore earned two college degrees from Old Dominion, in Human Services and Criminal Justice.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nbpa.com/kent-bazemore-from-small-town-kid-to-big-time-student-athlete-game-changer/ |title=Kent Bazemore: From Small-Town Kid to Big-Time Student-Athlete Game-Changer |access-date=July 28, 2018 |archive-date=July 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180728221415/https://nbpa.com/kent-bazemore-from-small-town-kid-to-big-time-student-athlete-game-changer/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Golden State Warriors (2012–2014)===
[[File:Kent Bazemore.jpg|thumb|upright|Bazemore with the Golden State Warriors in 2012]]
After going undrafted in the [[2012 NBA draft]], Bazemore joined the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for the Orlando Summer League and the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the Las Vegas Summer League. On July 26, he signed with Golden State.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/bazemore_signing_072612|title=Warriors Sign Rookie Free Agent Kent Bazemore|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 26, 2012|access-date=July 26, 2012}}</ref> During his rookie season, he was assigned multiple times to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html 2012-13 NBA Assignments] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327190108/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |date=March 27, 2014 }}</ref> On March 15, 2013, he scored a season-high 14 points in a loss to the Chicago Bulls.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bazemke01/gamelog/2013/ Kent Bazemore 2012-13 Game Log]</ref>

In July 2013, Bazemore re-joined Golden State for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]], where he was named a Summer League All-Tournament Team Recipient. The Warriors won the Summer League championship. On February 1, 2014, he was reassigned to the Santa Cruz Warriors.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-assign-bazemore-and-brooks-santa-cruz-warriors-nba-d-league Warriors Assign Bazemore and Brooks to Santa Cruz Warriors of NBA D-League]</ref> He was recalled by Golden State on February 2,<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/bazemore-brookes-recalled-from-santa-cruz-20140202 Warriors Recall Bazemore & Brooks From Santa Cruz Warriors of NBA D-League]</ref> reassigned on February 11,<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/bazemore-brooks-kuzimic-assigned-20140211 Warriors Assign Bazemore, Brooks, and Kuzmic to Santa Cruz Warriors of NBA D-League]</ref> and recalled again February 12.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/bazemore-brookes-kuzmic-recalled-from-santa-cruz-20140212 Warriors Recall Bazemore, Brooks & Kuzmic From Santa Cruz Of NBA D-League]</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2014)===
On February 19, 2014, Bazemore was traded, along with [[MarShon Brooks]], to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[Steve Blake]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140218bazemore_brooks_blake|title=Lakers Acquire Bazemore and Brooks|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=February 19, 2014|date=February 19, 2014}}</ref> On March 4, he tied his then career high of 23 points in a loss to the New Orleans Pelicans.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20140304/NOPLAL/gameinfo.html Notebook: Pelicans 132, Lakers 125]</ref> On April 7, he was ruled out of the rest of the season after suffering a torn tendon in his right foot.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140407kentbazemore Kent Bazemore Injury Update]</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2014–2019)===
[[File:1 kent bazemore 2015.jpg|thumb|upright|Bazemore taking a free-throw for Atlanta in a game against Washington in 2015]]
On September 23, 2014, Bazemore signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-sign-free-agent-guard-kent-bazemore Hawks Sign Free Agent Guard Kent Bazemore]</ref> On March 28, 2015, he scored a season-high 20 points in a 115–100 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150328/ATLCHA/gameinfo.html |title=Hornets beat Hawks backups 115-100 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=May 30, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151031074438/http://www.nba.com/games/20150328/ATLCHA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=October 31, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On November 7, 2015, Bazemore scored a career-high 25 points in a 114–99 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151107/WASATL/gameinfo.html |title=Hawks beat Wizards 114-99 for 7th straight win |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 8, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160113064649/http://www.nba.com/games/20151107/WASATL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 13, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 14, 2015, he set a new career high with 28 points in a 100–88 loss to the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151214/MIAATL/gameinfo.html |title=Bloodied but undaunted, Heat snap skid against Hawks 100-88 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=December 15, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160116152203/http://www.nba.com/games/20151214/MIAATL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 16, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On July 7, 2016, Bazemore re-signed with the Hawks on a four-year, $70 million contract.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-re-sign-kent-bazemore Hawks Re-Sign Kent Bazemore]</ref> On November 8, he scored a season-high 25 points against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. On January 23, 2017, Bazemore scored 25 points for a second time against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bazemke01/gamelog/2017/ Kent Bazemore 2016-17 Game Log]</ref>

On March 2, 2018, Bazemore scored a then career-high 29 points in a 114–109 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975674|title=Curry tweaks ankle, has 28 as Warriors top Hawks|work=ESPN.com|date=March 2, 2018|access-date=March 2, 2018}}</ref>

On October 24, 2018, Bazemore scored a career-high 32 points in a 111–104 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070733|title=Bazemore scores 32 points, Hawks rally to beat Mavs 111-104|work=ESPN.com|date=October 24, 2018|access-date=October 24, 2018}}</ref> On December 26, 2018, he tied a career high with 32 points in a 129–121 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071180|title=Young, Sabonis, Evans power Pacers past Hawks 129-121|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2018|access-date=December 27, 2018}}</ref>

On April 12, 2019, Bazemore exercised his $19.2 million player option for the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hawks-kent-bazemore-plans-to-exercise-option/|title=Hawks' Kent Bazemore: Plans to exercise option|work=CBSSports.com|date=April 12, 2019|access-date=April 12, 2019}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2019–2020)===
On June 24, 2019, Bazemore was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Evan Turner]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Trail Blazers Acquire Kent Bazemore From Atlanta in Exchange for Evan Turner |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-acquire-kent-bazemore-atlanta-exchange-evan-turner |website=NBA.com |access-date=June 24, 2019 |language=en}}</ref> He made his debut for the team on October 23, logging four points and five steals in a 100–108 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=JOKIC POWERS DENVER PAST PORTLAND 108-100 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900013 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2020)===
On January 20, 2020, Bazemore was traded, alongside [[Anthony Tolliver]] and two future second-round picks, to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Trevor Ariza]], [[Wenyen Gabriel]] and [[Caleb Swanigan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kings Acquire Kent Bazemore, Anthony Tolliver, 2024 and 2025 Second-Round Draft Selections |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-kent-bazemore-anthony-tolliver-2024-and-2025-second-round-draft-selections |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 21, 2020 |date=January 20, 2020}}</ref> Bazemore made his debut for the team two days later, scoring seven points in a 106–127 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ROSE, JACKSON LEAD PISTONS TO 127-106 ROUT OF REELING KINGS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900654 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Return to Golden State (2020–2021)===
On December 1, 2020, Bazemore signed a one-year contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]] to join the team for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Kent Bazemore|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/kent-bazemore-signing-20201201|website=NBA.com/warriors|date=December 1, 2020|access-date=December 1, 2020}}</ref> He made his debut for the team on December 22, logging two points, two rebounds and two assists in a 99–125 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DURANT RETURNS WITH 22 AND A 125-99 NETS ROUT OF WARRIORS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000001 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On February 17, 2021, Bazemore scored a season-high 26 points, alongside eight rebounds, three assists and three steals, in a 120–112 overtime win over the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CURRY AND HIS SUPPORTING CAST RALLY WARRIORS PAST HEAT IN OT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000443 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Return to the Lakers (2021–2022)===
On August 6, 2021, Bazemore signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Lakers Sign Kent Bazemore|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-kent-bazemore-2021|website=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021|access-date=August 6, 2021}}</ref> On January 28, 2022, he scored a season-high 13 points in a 114–117 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Reed|title=BRIDGES, HORNETS HOLD OFF SHORT-HANDED LAKERS, 117-114|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100735|website=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2023|access-date=January 29, 2023}}</ref>

On September 21, 2022, Bazemore signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Kent Bazemore and Quinn Cook|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-kent-bazemore-and-quinn-cook|website=NBA.com|date=September 21, 2022|access-date=September 21, 2022}}</ref> but was waived on October 13.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Waive Kent Bazemore and Quinn Cook|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-kent-bazemore-and-quinn-cook|website=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2022|access-date=January 22, 2023}}</ref>

On August 8, 2023, the [[Golden State Warriors]] held a free agent workout with Bazemore.<ref>{{cite tweet|first=Shams|last=Charania|title=The Warriors are holding free-agent workouts with veterans Dion Waiters, Tony Snell, Kent Bazemore, Juan Toscano-Anderson, Harry Giles and Trey Burke at facility over next two weeks, sources tell me and @anthonyVslater. GS has multiple round of workouts to identify signings.|number=1689068243040755712|user=ShamsCharania|date=August 8, 2023|access-date=August 9, 2023}}</ref>

===Greensboro Swarm (2024)===
On January 28, 2024, Bazemore joined the [[Greensboro Swarm]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Swarm Add Kent Bazemore to the Roster|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/swarm-add-kent-bazemore-to-the-roster|website=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2024|access-date=January 28, 2024}}</ref> However, he was waived on November 19.<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Greensboro Swarm Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Greensboro-Swarm/45/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 20, 2024}}</ref>

===Capital City Go-Go (2025)===
On March 24, 2025, the [[Capital City Go-Go]] announced that they had acquired Bazemore.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Capital City Go-Go|title=Official: We have acquired Kent Bazemore from the available G League player pool. Welcome to the Go-Go, Kent! #BeatOfDC|number=1904186020783886796|user=capitalcitygogo|date=March 24, 2025|access-date=March 24, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bazemore is a member of the [[Pi Kappa Alpha]] fraternity.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://kentbazemore20.com/about-kent/ |title=About Kent {{!}} KentBazemore20.com |access-date=January 29, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202094022/http://kentbazemore20.com/about-kent/ |archive-date=February 2, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> While with the Warriors, Bazemore was noted for his celebrations while on the team's bench, which became a fixture on [[YouTube]] and were included in the [[NBA 2K14]] video game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors rookie Kent Bazemore's bench celebrations are great|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/warriors-rookie-kent-bazemore-bench-celebrations-great-video-150605483--nba.html|website=Yahoo Sports|access-date=October 10, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Augustine|first1=Bermie|title=Kent Bazemore turns starring role on Warriors bench into feature in NBA 2K14|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/bazemoring-turns-warriors-super-sub-video-game-star-article-1.1450088|website=New York Daily News|access-date=October 10, 2014}}</ref> Kent married Samantha Serpe in Asheville, North Carolina in 2017;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://junebugweddings.com/wedding-blog/stunning-art-deco-inspired-biltmore-estate-wedding-north-carolina/|title = Stunning Art Deco Inspired Biltmore Estate Wedding in North Carolina | Junebug Weddings|date = October 10, 2017}}</ref> they were divorced in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bacardi |first=Francesca |date=2024-08-20 |title=Exclusive {{!}} NBA player Kent Bazemore paid ex Samantha $1.5M share of home in divorce |url=https://pagesix.com/2024/08/20/entertainment/nba-player-kent-bazemore-paid-ex-samantha-1-5m-share-of-home-in-divorce/ |access-date=2025-05-31 |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Role in Stephen Curry endorsement contract ===
In March 2016, [[ESPN]] writer Ethan Sherwood Strauss published a story about how [[Under Armour]] successfully signed away [[Stephen Curry]] from [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] in the 2013 offseason, and revealed that Bazemore played a significant role in the signing.

During the 2012 offseason, when Bazemore was an undrafted rookie trying to make the Warriors roster, his agent contacted Under Armour and convinced the company to take a chance on Bazemore as an endorser, noting that rising Warriors stars Curry and [[Klay Thompson]] had endorsement deals set to expire in the near future. Under Armour signed Bazemore to a deal, mainly providing massive amounts of branded merchandise—enough to allow Bazemore to provide clothing to several Warriors staff members. Once Bazemore made the team, he and his fellow North Carolinian Curry bonded over their common origins and shared work ethic. Bazemore then sold Curry on signing with Under Armour, which he did following several missteps by Nike. According to Strauss, "UA owes him [Bazemore] now. Big time." As a result, Bazemore has a six-figure deal with the company, an unusually high amount for a player of his stature in the league. The company also recognized Bazemore's role in luring Curry by signing an apparel deal with [[Old Dominion Monarchs and Lady Monarchs|Old Dominion]] for seven times the amount that the school had previously received from Nike. His deal with Under Armour enabled him to provide most of the funding for ODU's new basketball practice facility.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/15047018/how-nike-lost-stephen-curry-armour |title=You won't believe how Nike lost Steph to Under Armour |first=Ethan Sherwood |last=Strauss |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 24, 2016 |access-date=March 29, 2016}}</ref>
